description: A team of Cypress College students from the Psi Beta psychology honor society
summary: The Interplanetary Archive follows a Junior Archivist on a new mission. We developed a story-driven slide presentation that answers the “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” challenge by telling the stories of five NASA machines left behind on the Moon, Mars, an asteroid, and in deep space. Using real NASA mission history, the story shows how humanity’s abandoned machines still mark how far we’ve explored. These machines no longer operate, but they hold the history of human exploration.
details: We built The Interplanetary Archive as a story-driven slide presentation in Canva, using illustrated scenes, map transitions, and character dialogue to guide the audience from one stop to the next. To keep the story accurate, we used NASA resources and mission data for each artifact. The story begins when the Senior Archivist assigns Junior a new mission: five machines were built, launched, and left behind across the solar system without ever being properly archived. The Senior Archivist then hands Junior an old map marking each location, and Junior sets out to find every machine and bring its story home. His first stop is the Moon, where he finds the descent stage of Apollo 11’s lunar module, Eagle. In 1969, it carried Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin to the first crewed Moon landing, then served as a launch pad so its top half could carry them home. On Mars he finds the Opportunity rover, which was built to last about 90 days but kept exploring for nearly 15 years. Nearby is the Ingenuity helicopter, which was planned for 5 flights but completed 72, and which proved that powered flight is possible in an atmosphere only about 1% as dense as Earth’s. Next, on asteroid 433 Eros, he finds NEAR Shoemaker, which became the first spacecraft to land on an asteroid even though it was never designed to land at all. His final search follows a trail off the edge of his map to Pioneer 10. It launched in 1972, was the first spacecraft to cross the asteroid belt and fly past Jupiter, and has been traveling away from Earth for more than fifty years, long after its last signal reached us in 2003. At each stop, Junior learns how the machine got there, what it achieved, and why it was left behind, so the audience makes each discovery with him. Because the facts come through a character’s journey rather than a list, the presentation makes space history easier to follow and remember. Through our project, we hope to make sure these abandoned explorers are remembered.
